text: Cái bug này khó chịu thật, mình tìm cả buổi sáng mà chưa ra.
sample: This bug is driving me crazy — I've been digging into it all morning and still nothing.
note: “Driving me crazy” is the natural way to vent about something annoying.

text: Hóa ra vấn đề là do config sai chứ không phải code.
sample: It turns out the problem was a misconfig, not the code itself.
note: “It turns out” is the go-to opener for surprises.

text: The deploy failed at 5pm on Friday. Tell the team channel.
sample: Heads up — the deploy just failed. Looking into it now, will post updates here.
note: “Heads up” opens almost every alert message.

text: You disagree with a senior engineer’s approach in a code review. Push back politely.
sample: I might be missing something, but wouldn't this break if the list is empty?
chunk: I might be missing something, but...
note: The most powerful disagreement opener in English.

text: Your standup update: yesterday a bug fix, today a new task, no blockers.
sample: Quick one from me — wrapped up the login bug yesterday, picking up the export task today. No blockers.
note: Standup verbs: wrap up, pick up, look into, follow up.

text: Đáng lẽ mình nên review kỹ hơn trước khi merge.
sample: I should have reviewed it more carefully before merging.

text: Tính năng này nghe thì đơn giản nhưng làm thì phức tạp lắm.
sample: This feature sounds simple, but it's a lot trickier than it looks.

text: A recruiter asks: “Tell me about yourself” — give the 15-second version.
sample: I'm a developer based in Hanoi, mostly backend — I like taking messy systems and making them boring and reliable.

text: Cái này không gấp đâu, lúc nào rảnh thì làm.
sample: No rush on this — whenever you get a chance.

text: Your PM asks why the feature is taking longer than estimated.
sample: Honestly, it turned out messier than expected — the legacy code touches way more places than we thought.
note: “X than expected” saves you from word-by-word explanations.

text: Mình định nghỉ sớm hôm nay vì hơi mệt.
sample: I'm thinking of heading out early today — feeling a bit off.
note: “A bit off” covers tired, sick-ish, weird — all of it.

text: Dạo này mình toàn ngủ muộn, sáng dậy không nổi.
sample: I've been staying up way too late lately — mornings are a struggle.
note: “X is a struggle” — instant natural complaint.

text: Trời này mà được nằm nhà xem phim thì thích phải biết.
sample: Weather like this, I'd kill to just stay home and binge something.
note: “I’d kill to / I’d love to” = thích phải biết.

text: Your food delivery is 40 minutes late. Message the shipper without being rude.
sample: Hey, just checking in — any idea how far out you are? No worries if you're stuck in traffic.

text: Mình đang cố cắt giảm cà phê mà khó quá.
sample: I'm trying to cut back on coffee, but it's not going great.
note: Cut back on coffee, spending, screen time — endlessly reusable.

text: Explain to a foreign friend why crossing the street in Hanoi is an art form.
sample: The trick is to walk slowly and never stop — the bikes flow around you like water. Hesitate and you're done.
note: “The trick is to” opens any how-to explanation.

text: Cuối tuần này chắc mình ở nhà dọn dẹp với giặt giũ thôi.
sample: This weekend's probably just chores — cleaning, laundry, the usual.
note: Two words that end a sentence perfectly.

text: Mình quen làm việc buổi sáng hơn, đầu óc tỉnh táo hơn.
sample: I'm more of a morning person — my brain just works better before lunch.
note: “A tea person”, “a dog person” — endlessly reusable.

text: Your gym buddy asks why you skipped this week.
sample: Yeah, I fell off the wagon a bit — this week got away from me. Back on Monday, promise.
chunk: this week got away from me
note: The most forgiving excuse in English.

text: Để mai tính đi, giờ muộn rồi.
sample: Let's deal with it tomorrow — it's getting late.
note: “Deal with” = xử lý, giải quyết, tính. One verb, many jobs.

text: Small talk: a coworker asks how your weekend was. It was boring.
sample: Pretty quiet, honestly — just caught up on sleep and watched stuff. Needed it though.
note: You don’t need an exciting weekend, just a natural-sounding one.

text: Recommend your favorite phở place to a foreign coworker visiting Hanoi.
sample: You've got to try this place near my office — best broth in the Old Quarter, hands down.

text: Decline a friend’s invitation to go out tonight — you just don’t feel like it.
sample: I'm gonna pass tonight — not really feeling it. Rain check?
note: One word-pair that means “lần khác nhé” without guilt.

text: Lâu lắm rồi không gặp, dạo này thế nào?
sample: Hey, it's been ages! How've you been?
note: Greeting chunk. Fires automatically once memorized.

text: Someone compliments your English. Respond without the awkward deny-everything reflex.
sample: Ah, thanks — still a work in progress, but I'm getting there.
note: Accepts the compliment AND stays humble. Perfect.

text: Thôi để mình trả tiền lần này, lần sau bạn mời.
sample: This one's on me — you can get the next one.

text: You forgot a person’s name two minutes after they introduced themselves. Recover.
sample: I'm so sorry, your name slipped my mind — I'm terrible with names the first time.
note: “Slipped my mind” works for names, deadlines, birthdays...

text: Nghe hấp dẫn đấy, kể thêm đi.
sample: Ooh, that sounds interesting — tell me more.
note: The two most powerful small-talk words. People love talking.

text: End a conversation politely because you need to leave.
sample: Anyway, I should get going — it was really good catching up!
note: The universal polite exit. “Anyway” signals the landing.

text: Mình không phản đối, nhưng mình nghĩ nên cân nhắc thêm rủi ro.
sample: I'm not against it — I just think we should weigh the risks a bit more.
chunk: I'm not against it, I just...
note: Disagreement without conflict. Gold in any debate.

text: Càng nghĩ càng thấy giải pháp này không ổn.
sample: The more I think about it, the more this feels wrong.
note: A pattern chunk — memorize the shape, swap the words.

text: Hot take time: is AI going to replace developers? Honest opinion, 2 sentences.
sample: Honestly, I think it replaces tasks, not developers — the job just shifts up a level. The people in trouble are the ones who refuse to use it.
note: “Honestly” buys you a second to think AND sounds confident.

text: Theo mình thì tiền không mua được hạnh phúc, nhưng thiếu tiền thì chắc chắn khổ.
sample: The way I see it, money can't buy happiness — but not having it definitely buys misery.
note: Opinion opener that sounds thoughtful, not aggressive.

text: A friend says remote work is dead. You disagree. Argue back, friendly.
sample: I don't know, man — companies keep saying that, but every good dev I know still gets remote offers.
note: Casual disagreement starts soft, then lands the punch.

text: Cũng tùy thôi, mỗi người một kiểu mà.
sample: It really depends — different strokes for different folks.
note: The honest answer to half of all questions.

text: Rank: bánh mì vs phở vs bún chả. Defend your #1 like it matters.
sample: Bún chả, no contest — it's got the smoke, the herbs, the dipping ritual. Phở is comfort, but bún chả is an event.
note: “No contest” = không cần so. Confidence in two words.

text: Nói thật là mình thấy phim đó hơi bị đánh giá quá cao.
sample: Honestly? I think that movie is kind of overrated.
note: “Kind of” softens any spicy opinion just enough.

text: Tell the story of the worst bug you ever shipped — 3 sentences, make it dramatic.
sample: So picture this: Friday night, everyone's gone home, and I push one tiny fix. Turns out that tiny fix logged every user out of the entire app. I spent the weekend pretending my phone was broken.
note: “Picture this” makes any story instantly cinematic.

text: Suýt nữa thì mình xóa nhầm database production.
sample: I almost dropped the production database by accident.
note: No “suýt nữa thì” gymnastics — just “almost did”.

text: Describe your first day at your current job — one funny or awkward detail.
sample: My first day, I spent twenty minutes looking for the meeting room before realizing it was the glass box I'd been standing next to the whole time.
note: “The whole time” is the punchline chunk of English.

text: Đang giữa chừng cuộc họp thì mất điện, thế là cả phòng ngồi cười.
sample: We were right in the middle of the meeting when the power went out — the whole room just burst out laughing.
note: Emotion verbs: burst out laughing, break down crying, light up.

text: Tell a foreigner about a Tết tradition in your family — story, not Wikipedia.
sample: Every year my mom wakes the whole house up at dawn to clean — apparently luck doesn't visit messy homes. We complain every single year, and every single year we do it anyway.
note: Repetition chunk that makes stories feel alive.

text: Lúc đó mình chẳng biết phải làm gì, đành cứ liều thôi.
sample: At that point I had no idea what to do, so I just winged it.
note: “Wing it” = liều / làm đại. Beautiful little verb.

text: You ran into an old classmate unexpectedly. Tell a friend what happened.
sample: You won't believe who I bumped into at the coffee shop — we ended up talking for like an hour, totally out of nowhere.
note: “Bump into” = tình cờ gặp. “Run into” works too.

text: Chuyến đi đó đáng nhớ lắm, có cả trận mưa to nhất mình từng thấy.
sample: That trip was unforgettable — we got caught in the heaviest rain I've ever seen.

text: Thôi kệ đi, không đáng để cãi nhau vì chuyện đó.
sample: Ah, let it go — it's not worth arguing over.
note: “Not worth doing X” covers a hundred Vietnamese sentences.

text: Để mình xem lại rồi báo bạn sau nhé.
sample: Let me double-check and get back to you.
note: One chunk replaces a whole word-by-word sentence.

text: Your teammate asks you to join a call in 5 minutes, but you are mid-debugging.
sample: Can we push it back like 15 minutes? I'm right in the middle of something.

text: Dạo này mình hơi bận nên chưa trả lời tin nhắn được.
sample: Sorry, things have been a bit hectic lately — just catching up on messages now.

text: Nếu mình là bạn thì mình sẽ hỏi sếp trước cho chắc.
sample: If I were you, I'd run it by the boss first, just to be safe.
note: “Run it by X” = hỏi ý kiến X. Pure native.

text: Mình nghĩ ta nên gộp hai task này lại cho đỡ mất thời gian.
sample: I think we should just roll these two tasks into one — save ourselves the back-and-forth.
note: “Roll into” = gộp lại. Cleaner than “combine together”.

text: A teammate keeps interrupting you in meetings. Raise it with them privately, kindly.
sample: Hey, can I flag something small? I sometimes lose my train of thought when I get cut off — mind letting me finish first?
note: Names the problem without blaming. Pure native phrasing.

text: Chỗ này mình chưa chắc lắm, để mình hỏi lại cho chắc.
sample: I'm not 100% on this part — let me confirm before we move forward.
note: Honest uncertainty without sounding lost. Dev gold.

text: You need a deadline extension. Ask your manager without sounding like you slacked off.
sample: The scope grew more than we planned — could I get a couple more days to do it properly rather than rush it?
chunk: do it properly rather than rush it
note: Frames extra time as quality, not delay.

text: Cái này để mình lo, bạn cứ tập trung phần của bạn đi.
sample: I've got this one — you just focus on your side.
note: Three words that take ownership instantly.

text: Onboarding a new hire: tell them it’s fine to ask “dumb” questions.
sample: Seriously, ask me anything — there are no dumb questions in your first month. I'd rather you ask than guess.
note: “I’d rather ask than guess” — reusable preference shape.

text: Đợt này nhiều việc quá, mình hơi đuối rồi.
sample: It's been a lot lately — I'm stretched pretty thin, to be honest.
note: Professional way to say “overloaded” without complaining.

text: Decline extra work politely when your plate is already full.
sample: I'd love to help, but I'm pretty maxed out this sprint — can it wait, or should we find someone else?
note: “Maxed out” = hết công suất. Sets a boundary nicely.

text: Nói chung là chạy được rồi, còn vài chỗ nhỏ cần dọn lại.
sample: Basically it works — just a few rough edges left to clean up.
note: “Rough edges” = chỗ chưa hoàn thiện. Very natural.

text: Sáng nay kẹt xe kinh khủng, mình đứng yên cả hai mươi phút.
sample: Traffic was brutal this morning — I was stuck at a standstill for like twenty minutes.

text: You burned dinner and have to decide what to do. Talk it through out loud.
sample: Well, that's ruined — let's just order in. I'm not cooking twice tonight.
note: “Order in” = gọi đồ ăn về nhà. Two words.

text: Điện thoại mình sắp hết pin rồi, lát nữa mất sóng đừng lo nhé.
sample: My phone's about to die — if I go quiet, that's why.
note: For phones/batteries, “die” is the natural verb.

text: Dạo này mình tập đi ngủ sớm, thấy người khỏe hẳn.
sample: I've been getting to bed earlier lately, and honestly it's made a huge difference.
note: Closes any “I changed X and now Y” story.

text: A neighbor’s dog won’t stop barking at night. Ask them to help, staying friendly.
sample: Hey, no big deal, but I've been having trouble sleeping — any chance we could keep Max in at night?
note: Softest possible way to make a request.

text: Thôi hôm nay tự thưởng cho mình một bữa ngon đi.
sample: You know what, let's treat ourselves to something nice tonight.
note: “Treat yourself” = tự thưởng. Reuse it weekly.

text: Mình hay quên mang ô, kiểu gì hôm nào quên là hôm đó mưa.
sample: I always forget my umbrella — and of course it pours the one day I do.
note: Sarcastic “of course” for life’s little ironies.

text: You’re trying to cut spending. Talk yourself out of an impulse buy.
sample: Do I actually need this, or do I just want it? ...Yeah, I'll sleep on it.
note: “Sleep on it” = để mai tính. Buys you a decision.

text: Cuối cùng cũng xong việc nhà, giờ mới được ngồi thở.
sample: Finally done with the chores — now I can actually sit down and breathe.
note: “Finally + done with” opens any relief sentence.

text: Congratulate a friend who just got a new job.
sample: That's amazing, congrats! You totally earned it — when do you start?

text: Để mình giới thiệu, đây là Minh, bạn cùng công ty mình.
sample: Oh, let me introduce you — this is Minh, I work with him.
note: The clean way to bridge two people. Memorize whole.

text: You’re late meeting a friend. Send a quick, light apology text.
sample: So sorry, running about ten behind — grab us a table and I'll be right there!
note: “Running X behind” = trễ X phút. Native shorthand.

text: Hôm nay vui quá, lần sau làm tiếp nhé!
sample: Today was so much fun — we've got to do this again soon!
chunk: we've got to do this again
note: The standard warm goodbye. Fires on autopilot.

text: A friend is venting about a bad day. Respond supportively without fixing it.
sample: Ugh, that sounds rough — I'm sorry. You want to talk about it, or just vent?
note: Validates first. Don’t jump to solutions.

text: Bạn ăn thử miếng này đi, ngon lắm, mình bao!
sample: Here, you've got to try this — it's so good. On me, don't worry.

text: Someone you barely know asks to borrow money. Decline gracefully.
sample: Ah, I'm a bit tight myself right now — wish I could help. Hope it works out though.
chunk: I'm a bit tight right now
note: Soft money-decline that saves face for both.

text: Lâu rồi không tụ tập, cuối tuần này cà phê không?
sample: It's been forever — you free for a coffee this weekend?
note: Casual invite shape. Swap coffee for anything.

text: You disagree with a friend’s plan but don’t want a fight. Soften it.
sample: Hmm, I see where you're coming from, but I'm not sure it'll work — can I throw out another idea?
chunk: I see where you're coming from
note: Acknowledges them before you push back. Disarming.

text: Không sao đâu, ai mà chẳng có lúc như vậy.
sample: Don't worry about it — it happens to the best of us.
chunk: it happens to the best of us
note: Comforts anyone who messed up. Pure warmth.

text: Hot take: is working from home making people lazier? Two sentences, be honest.
sample: Honestly, I think it exposes people, not changes them — lazy folks were always lazy, they just had an office to hide in. Discipline is the real variable, not location.
note: Reframes the debate instead of picking a side. Sounds sharp.

text: Mình thấy học tiếng Anh quan trọng nhất là dám nói sai.
sample: For me, the biggest thing in learning English is being willing to sound stupid.
note: “Willing to” = dám / sẵn sàng. Endlessly reusable.

text: A friend swears expensive phones aren’t worth it. You half-agree. Nuance it.
sample: I'm with you up to a point — past a certain price you're just paying for the logo, but a good camera does change how much I actually use it.
chunk: I'm with you up to a point
note: Agree-then-qualify. The mark of a thoughtful answer.

text: Theo mình, thà làm chậm mà chắc còn hơn nhanh mà ẩu.
sample: The way I see it, slow and solid beats fast and sloppy every time.
note: Punchy comparison chunk. Drop in any two options.

text: Is it rude to text during dinner? Give your honest position.
sample: I'll be honest, it bugs me a little — but I get that some people are just on call. Depends on the situation, I guess.
note: Mild annoyance without sounding harsh. Very native.

text: Mình nghĩ tiền tiết kiệm quan trọng, nhưng trải nghiệm cũng đáng tiền.
sample: I think saving matters, but some experiences are worth every penny.
note: “Worth every penny” = đáng đồng tiền. Locks in approval.

text: Someone says AI art isn’t “real” art. Take a side, casually.
sample: Eh, I'm on the fence — the tool doesn't bother me, but I do care who's pointing it and why.
note: “On the fence” = chưa ngả về bên nào. Honest middle ground.

text: Nói thật, mình thấy mạng xã hội lợi bất cập hại.
sample: Honestly, I think social media does more harm than good.
note: Clean verdict phrase. Flip it: “more good than harm”.

text: Defend a slightly embarrassing thing you love (a guilty-pleasure show, snack...).
sample: Look, I know it's trash, but that's exactly why I love it — sometimes you don't want to think, you just want to watch.
note: Owning the take is funnier than hiding it.

text: Mình cho rằng thất bại không sao, miễn là rút được kinh nghiệm.
sample: I'd say failing is fine, as long as you take something away from it.
note: “Take away from” = rút ra. Mature, reflective tone.

text: Is money or passion more important in a job? Pick one and commit.
sample: Passion pays the soul, money pays the rent — but if I had to pick, I'd chase something I don't dread on Monday.
note: Forces a clear stance after the nuance. Confident close.

text: Tell the story of the most embarrassing typo you ever sent at work. Make it sting.
sample: So I meant to type 'Best, Nam' to a client — autocorrect made it 'Beast, Nam'. They replied 'Rawr 🐯' and somehow we've been friends ever since.
note: The twist verb “somehow” turns disasters into stories.

text: Hồi nhỏ mình từng trốn học đi chơi điện tử, bị mẹ bắt tại trận.
sample: As a kid I once skipped school for the arcade — and my mom caught me red-handed.
note: “Red-handed” = bắt tại trận. Perfect for childhood crimes.

text: Describe a trip that went completely wrong but turned out memorable.
sample: Everything that could go wrong did — missed the bus, lost a bag, got rained on — and yet it's the trip I talk about the most.
chunk: everything that could go wrong did
note: The ultimate travel-disaster opener. Sets up the “and yet”.

text: Mình đợi mãi mới tới lượt, vừa tới quầy thì hết hàng.
sample: I waited forever for my turn, and the second I reached the counter — sold out.
note: “The second I X, Y” = vừa mới X thì Y. Builds comic timing.

text: Tell about a time a stranger did something unexpectedly kind.
sample: I was short on cash at the register, fumbling, and the guy behind me just covered it — wouldn't even let me pay him back. Restored my faith a bit.
note: Warm story-closer. Ties the moment to a feeling.

text: Lần đầu đi phỏng vấn mình run đến mức quên cả tên công ty.
sample: At my first-ever interview I was so nervous I blanked on the company's name.
note: “Blank on” = quên sạch. Better than “forgot suddenly”.

text: Recount the moment you realized you were finally getting good at something.
sample: One day it just clicked — I stopped translating in my head and the words were suddenly there. That's when I knew I'd turned a corner.
note: “Clicked” + “turned a corner” = the breakthrough story combo.

text: Hôm đó mưa to, hai đứa phải trú dưới mái hiên cả tiếng đồng hồ.
sample: It poured that day, so the two of us ended up sheltering under an awning for a solid hour.
note: “A solid hour” = nguyên một tiếng. Adds weight to time.

text: Tell about a small risk you took that paid off.
sample: I almost didn't send that message — and I'm so glad I did, because that one text basically changed everything.
note: Near-miss framing makes any outcome feel earned.

text: Mình tưởng dễ ăn, ai ngờ làm cả ngày mới xong.
sample: I thought it'd be a piece of cake — turns out it took me all day.
note: “Piece of cake” = dễ ợt. The irony sets up the story.

text: Describe the worst meal you’ve ever had — vividly, in two sentences.
sample: Picture grey noodles in water that had clearly given up. I took one bite, smiled politely, and quietly planned my escape.

text: Mình cần thêm chút thời gian để review cái PR này cho kỹ.
sample: I'll need a bit more time to give this PR a proper review.
note: “Give it a proper X” = do X thoroughly, not rushed.

text: Task này phụ thuộc vào team backend nên mình đang bị kẹt.
sample: I'm blocked on this — it depends on the backend team.
note: “Blocked on X” is standup gold for dependencies.

text: Để mình ghi nhanh vào ticket cho khỏi quên.
sample: Let me jot that down in the ticket so it doesn't slip.

text: Hình như lỗi này lọt vào do merge nhầm branch.
sample: I think this bug crept in from a bad merge.

text: Mình đẩy lên staging trước rồi test cho chắc.
sample: I'll push it to staging first and test it just to be safe.

text: Đợt này việc nhiều quá, mình hơi đuối.
sample: It's been full-on lately — I'm a bit swamped.

text: Mình nghĩ estimate này hơi lạc quan.
sample: I think this estimate is a little optimistic.

text: Your teammate's PR has a bug but they clearly worked hard. Point it out kindly.
sample: Really solid work overall — one thing: I think it breaks when the input is null.
note: Lead with praise, then “one thing” softens the catch.

text: You're going to miss a deadline. Tell your manager early and honestly.
sample: Heads up — I don't think I'll hit Friday. I'd rather flag it now than surprise you later.
note: Owning a slip early builds trust.

text: Ask a senior dev for help without sounding helpless.
sample: Got a sec? I've been poking at this for an hour and want a second pair of eyes.
note: Frames help as a sanity check, not a rescue.

text: Decline extra work politely because you're already overloaded.
sample: I'd love to, but my plate's pretty full this sprint — can it wait till next?

text: Explain why you chose a simpler solution over a fancy one.
sample: I went with the boring option on purpose — easier to maintain and it does the job.

text: Give a one-line intro before demoing a feature you built.
sample: So here's the gist: you click here, it auto-fills the rest. Let me walk you through it.

text: A new teammate asks where to start. Point them in the right direction.
sample: Best first step? Get the project running locally — ping me if anything breaks.

text: Sáng nay kẹt xe kinh khủng, mình tới trễ.
sample: Traffic was brutal this morning — I'm running late.

text: Mình ăn gì cũng được, bạn chọn đi.
sample: I'm easy — you pick.
note: “I'm easy” = I don't mind either way.

text: Cuối tuần mình chẳng làm gì, chỉ ở nhà nghỉ.
sample: I did nothing all weekend — just chilled at home.

text: Dạo này mình tập gym đều hơn rồi.
sample: I've been hitting the gym more regularly lately.

text: Cà phê ở đây ngon mà hơi đắt.
sample: The coffee here's great, just a bit pricey.
